items.title: NexStox & NXMarket Trading Platforms
items.subtitle: Fintech Trading & Staking Platforms
items.description: Owned the frontend of two live fintech platforms — both the user-facing apps and their admin panels — shipping staking, Launchpad, KYC, and a brand-new platform, and testing every feature end to end from admin to user.

overview.label: Role
overview.value: Senior Frontend Engineer · sole frontend engineer for the first 3 months

overview.label: Team
overview.value: 1–3 frontend engineers, working with Product, Backend, QA, and DevOps

overview.label: Scope
overview.value: Trading, staking, Launchpad, sign-up & KYC, admin panel and API integration, multilingual UI

items.context: NexStox and NXMarket are two fintech platforms where users trade digital assets, stake to earn rewards, and invest in new projects through a Launchpad. Each platform has two sides: an **admin panel** where the operations team configures staking pools, Launchpad projects, and KYC reviews, and the **user app** where customers act on them. I joined as the **only frontend engineer** and owned both sides — from reading the product spec to verifying the feature in production.

challenges.title: Two platforms, two sides each
challenges.body: For the first three months I was the only frontend engineer. Every feature had to be built twice over — configured in the admin panel, consumed in the user app — on two platforms, with deadlines that did not move.

challenges.title: Money rules users have to trust
challenges.body: Staking combined single and compound rewards, stake-more, unstaking, and early-withdrawal penalties. Any gap between what the screen showed and what the backend calculated would cost users money — and the product its credibility.

challenges.title: A new platform without starting over
challenges.body: The business needed NXMarket launched on top of the existing product, with its own UI, sign-up and KYC flows, and multiple languages — without destabilizing the platform users already relied on.

challenges.title: An unstable exchange interface
challenges.body: The new exchange interface had critical issues in key trading workflows — the part of the product users touch most and tolerate failure least.

solutions.title: From spec to shipped feature, in the open
solutions.body: Each feature started from the Product Owner's document. I read it end to end, then **discussed it with the backend team and the designer** — agreeing on API contracts, edge cases, and UI states — before implementing, and went back to them whenever a feature needed updating.

solutions.title: Owned the admin panel as well as the user app
solutions.body: Alongside the user-facing apps, I built the admin screens and **integrated their APIs** — creating and configuring staking pools and Launchpad projects, and reviewing and approving KYC submissions — so every feature was complete on both sides.

solutions.title: Modelled every staking state before building screens
solutions.body: I mapped the full lifecycle — **single and compound rewards, stake, stake-more, unstake, and penalties** — and built the flows around it, so users could see exactly what would happen to their funds before confirming.

images.caption: Pool position with dividends and rewards

solutions.title: Built the new platform from the proven core
solutions.body: I adapted the existing product's core functionality for NXMarket, then added the **new UI, sign-up and KYC flows, and multilingual support** on top, reusing logic that already worked rather than rebuilding it.

images.caption: Profile with KYC and security status

solutions.title: Tested every feature end to end, admin to user
solutions.body: I didn't stop at my own screens. For each feature I ran the **full flow**: create a staking pool or Launchpad project in the admin panel, or submit a KYC application and approve it there — then switch to the user app and verify that what users see and can do matches what was configured.

solutions.title: Thought like a product owner, as a team
solutions.body: Our team worked with a shared rule: **everyone acts as a product owner**. We set aside time to use the product ourselves, walking features from admin to user to hunt for bugs and **propose improvements** to existing features — not just wait for tickets.

solutions.title: Stabilized trading together with QA
solutions.body: I traced and fixed critical issues in the exchange interface, and worked closely with QA — often past working hours — on platform testing and the **accuracy of data shown on screen** before every release.

metrics.label: platforms, each with an admin panel and a user app
major modules shipped: staking, Launchpad, sign-up & KYC, multilingual UI, and a new platform

impact.summary: Staking, Launchpad, and the new NXMarket platform reached production on schedule, and key trading workflows became noticeably more stable. In his letter of recommendation, the company's President described it as **one person running an entire frontend department on her own**.

learnings: **Ownership lives in the gaps.** When specs, designs, and APIs disagree, the frontend engineer is usually the first to notice — raising it early is cheaper than fixing it after release.
**In fintech, accuracy is the feature.** Testing the numbers on screen with QA mattered as much as the UI around them.
**Test the whole loop, not just the screen.** Creating a pool in admin and watching it reach users catches bugs that no single-screen review ever would.
**Reuse beats rewrite** when the boundary between shared and new behaviour is clear — it is how a second platform shipped without slowing the first.

items.title: E-Learning Platform
items.subtitle: Learning Management Platform
items.description: Set up the frontend from an empty repository and built the core student experience — a multi-format lesson player plus real-time comments and notifications.

overview.label: Role
overview.value: Frontend Engineer · owned the frontend architecture from day one

overview.label: Scope
overview.value: Monorepo setup, lesson player, real-time comments and notifications

items.context: A learning platform where students watch lessons, read course material, and discuss it with teachers and classmates. I started from an **empty repository** and was responsible for both the frontend foundation and the features students use every day.

challenges.title: Starting from nothing
challenges.body: There was no existing structure. Early decisions about the repository and architecture would shape how quickly — and how safely — every later feature could be built.

challenges.title: Many ways to learn in one place
challenges.body: Video, book mode, subtitles, chapters, pages, and bookmarks all had to work together, so learners could switch formats and pick up exactly where they left off.

challenges.title: Social features that feel live
challenges.body: Comments, likes, teacher replies, and notifications had to update in real time, without the learning content and the social layer drifting out of sync.

solutions.title: A monorepo foundation built to grow
solutions.body: I set up the **entire monorepo architecture from scratch**, giving the team a consistent structure to add features on from the first sprint.

solutions.title: One player, every format
solutions.body: I built the learning experience around a single player supporting **video, book mode, subtitles, chapters, pages, and bookmarking**, so students choose how they learn without leaving the lesson.

solutions.title: Real-time discussion with a clear thread model
solutions.body: I built a real-time commenting system with **comments, likes, and one-level teacher replies**, which keeps answers from teachers easy to find inside busy discussions.

solutions.title: Notifications and data kept in sync
solutions.body: I developed real-time notifications with their own interactions, and integrated **REST APIs with real-time data flows** so learning progress and social activity stayed consistent.

metrics.label: frontend architecture and monorepo built from scratch
learning tools in one player: video, book mode, subtitles, chapters, pages, bookmarks
comments, likes, teacher replies, and notifications

impact.summary: Students got one place to learn in the format that suits them and to discuss lessons with teachers as they happen — on a codebase structured to keep growing.

learnings: **Foundations compound.** Time spent on the monorepo up front paid back on every feature that followed.
**Real-time is a data problem before it is a UI problem.** Deciding what syncs, and when, made the interface simple.

items.title: Aimee by J — Headless Ecommerce Storefront
items.subtitle: Vietnamese Fashion Ecommerce · In Progress
items.description: An independent, ground-up headless commerce build for a Vietnamese fashion brand — a Next.js 16 storefront on a Medusa v2 backend, designed for reliability and local payments.

overview.label: Scope
overview.value: Architecture, data layer, rendering strategy, payments, and delivery roadmap

items.context: Aimee by J is a Vietnamese fashion brand. I am rebuilding its storefront as a **headless commerce stack**, owning every layer — from backend and storefront architecture to the delivery plan.

challenges.title: Two systems that must evolve independently
challenges.body: The storefront and the commerce backend needed to change and deploy on their own schedules, without breaking each other.

challenges.title: API failures that silently break pages
challenges.body: A failed or empty API response that slips through can quietly corrupt a page render — the kind of bug customers notice before developers do.

challenges.title: Checkout that fits the Vietnamese market
challenges.body: Local shoppers expect Cash on Delivery and local payment gateways such as PayOS and VNPay — not only international cards.

solutions.title: A fully decoupled headless stack
solutions.body: The **Next.js 16 storefront consumes Medusa v2 purely through its REST API**, so either side can evolve independently.

solutions.title: Errors as values, not exceptions
solutions.body: I designed a typed HTTP data layer around a **discriminated-union Result type**, so every page must handle failure explicitly and a bad response cannot slip through unnoticed.

solutions.title: Fixed a production build at its root
solutions.body: I traced a build failure to Next.js's **static-vs-dynamic rendering boundary** and moved a backend-dependent route from build-time prerendering to request-time rendering.

solutions.title: Local payments and a realistic roadmap
solutions.body: I planned **Cash on Delivery and a custom PayOS/VNPay payment provider** on Medusa's payment architecture, and mapped delivery phase by phase with time estimates and a testing strategy using Vitest, React Testing Library, and Playwright.

metrics.label: independently deployable apps: storefront and commerce backend
of API calls return a typed Result the page must handle
testing layers planned: unit, component, and end-to-end

impact.summary: The project is still in progress. So far it has a reliable, decoupled foundation and a clear path to a checkout built for Vietnamese shoppers.

learnings: **Make failure impossible to ignore.** Encoding errors in types moved a whole class of bugs from production to compile time.
**Know where your framework renders.** Understanding Next.js's rendering boundary turned a confusing build failure into a one-line fix.

items.title: English with J — Active Listening Platform
items.subtitle: English Learning Platform · In Progress
items.description: An independent English-learning platform that turns every listening lesson into active practice — dictation, AI-generated IELTS/TOEIC quizzes, personalised mistake feedback, and karaoke-style shadowing.

overview.label: Role
overview.value: Sole developer — product, design, and frontend

overview.label: Scope
overview.value: Sign-up & login, the listening practice flow, AI quizzes and feedback, saved progress, and a bilingual interface

items.context: Most English learners practise listening by replaying audio and hoping it sticks. English with J is a platform I am building to make listening **active**: each lesson guides the learner from understanding the gist, to writing down every sentence, to testing comprehension, to speaking along. Phase 1 focuses on that core listening experience, accounts, and saved progress.

challenges.title: Passive listening doesn't build skill
challenges.body: Replaying a recording feels like practice, but without writing, checking, and speaking, learners rarely find out what they actually missed.

challenges.title: Feedback that is specific enough to act on
challenges.body: A single score says little. Learners need to see which words they misheard, what each part means, and which mistakes they keep repeating.

challenges.title: A free tier that sells, and a paywall that holds
challenges.body: New learners should be able to try real lessons before paying, while paid lessons stay locked to anyone who hasn't paid — no matter what the browser shows.

solutions.title: A seven-step listening flow
solutions.body: Every lesson follows the same path: **listen for the gist → write down the main ideas → dictate part by part → answer an AI-generated quiz → get a score → review common mistakes → shadow the script**. Each step builds on the one before, so learners finish a lesson having listened, written, understood, and spoken.

solutions.title: Dictation with instant, part-by-part checking
solutions.body: Learners type what they hear for each part of the recording. The platform **checks each answer against the script**, highlights what is right and wrong, and shows a **Vietnamese translation** alongside. They can **save a note on any part**, and switch on **voice mode** to fill the text box by speaking instead of typing.

solutions.title: AI quizzes and personalised mistake feedback
solutions.body: After dictation, AI creates **IELTS- and TOEIC-style questions** based on that lesson to test real comprehension, then scores the answers. It then **analyses the learner's mistakes** to point out the patterns they fall into most often.

solutions.title: Karaoke-style shadowing to finish the lesson
solutions.body: The final step is a video of the script that **scrolls up line by line like karaoke**, with a voice reading it aloud — so learners can watch, listen, and **shadow** the speaker to practise pronunciation and rhythm.

solutions.title: Free preview and backend-checked access
solutions.body: Learners can open a few sample lessons before choosing a paid plan. The interface reflects the learner's plan, but **access to every paid lesson is checked by the backend**, so hiding a lock icon never unlocks content.

solutions.title: Saved progress and a bilingual interface
solutions.body: Signed-in learners pick up where they left off, with their progress and notes saved to their account. The interface is available in **English and Vietnamese**, and the code is organised by feature so each part of the lesson flow can grow on its own.

metrics.label: steps in every listening lesson, from first listen to shadowing
a few open lessons, with full-library access on a paid plan

impact.summary: The project is still in progress. Phase 1 defines a complete listening loop, from first listen to speaking along, with accounts and saved progress. Its foundation is ready for lessons and quizzes to be added step by step.

learnings: **Design the learning loop before the screens.** Mapping all seven steps first made it clear what each screen must hand to the next.
**The frontend shows access; the backend decides it.** Keeping paid access checks on the server keeps the paywall reliable without making the interface complicated.
